newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Hundreds of foreigners evacuated from Albania.
newsitem.headline: Hundreds of foreigners evacuated from Albania.

text.p: The United States, Italy and Britain evacuated hundreds of foreigners from Albania on Friday by air and sea as the tiny Balkan country slid further towards anarchy.

U.S. helicopters began ferrying American nationals away from the capital Tirana on Friday morning, and an embassy spokesman said up to 2,200 people with American and dual nationality could be involved.
"We don't know how many of those will want to leave," Charles Walsh told Reuters. "We know that some have expressed a wish to stay."
He said the operation would continue for as long as was needed. U.S. sources said that it might have to be continued on Saturday.
The helicopters involved, Sea Knight and Sea Stallions with two-man Cobras providing security, were from the U.S. navy amphibious ships Nassau, Nashville and Pensacola in the Adriatic.
A spokesman for the U.S. navy said it was not clear where the evacuees would be taken, although the likeliest destination was the Italian port of Brindisi.
Earlier in the day six Italian military helicopters, including giant Chinooks, swooped down on Tirana's main football stadium and lifted off around 100 Italians and others.

The Italian Foreign Minister said it had completed an evacuation begun on Thursday, in which a total of some 1,000 Italians, other foreigners and a small number of Albanians have been taken out of the country by air and sea.
Around 130 British, Commonwealth and European nationals were evacuated on Friday morning from the port of Durres, about 30 km (20 miles) west of Tirana, by an Italian navy vessel to Brindisi.
The evacuees arrived in the port on Thursday but were forced to spend the night on the beach after the Italian captain was unable to land because of the chaotic situation in the port.
In Durres, as in virtually all parts of the country, the army and police have melted away and civilians have looted military barracks of weapons, firing them into the air.
At least 10 more Britons spent Thursday night at the British embassy in the Albanian capital.

Diplomats were waiting to see how many more responded to an appeal broadcast on BBC World Service radio for British citizens to present themselves at the embassy before arranging another evacuation effort, the spokesman said.
A further group of around 100 from countries including Germany, Austria and Greece, were gathered at the Austrian embassy in Tirana waiting for transport to take them to Durres.
Albanian authorities, buoyed by a new all-party government, have appealed unsuccessfully for calm against a campaign by rebels demanding the resignation of President Sali Berisha.
